### Exercise 5.7: Use positive and negative numbers to solve problems.

2. A piece of meat is at a room temperature of 25\space ^\circ \text C. It is placed in a freezer. The temperature of the meat drops by 40\space ^\circ \text C. Calculate the new temperature of the meat.
records.answer_text:
If the temperature dropped, we must count 40 units in the negative direction: 25\space ^\circ \text C +(- 40\space ^\circ \text C)

Start at the number +25.

Count 25 units in the negative direction. Now you are at zero.

Count another 40-25=15 units in the negative direction. Now you are at -15.

The new temperature is -15\space ^\circ \text C.

records.raw_html:
• The place value of a digit tells us what the value of that digit is, based on its position in a number.
  • When we add or subtract large numbers, we line up the units, tens, hundreds and thousands of the numbers.
  • A number line is a straight line, divided into equal segments, that shows the positions of numbers.
  • Positive numbers are larger than zero and lie to the right of zero on a number line.
  • Negative numbers are smaller than zero and lie to the left of zero on a number line.
  • Zero is neither positive nor negative.
  • The symbol < means "smaller than", and 3<5 means three is smaller than five. The symbol > means "greater than", and 5>3 means five is greater than three.
  • When we add one integer to another, we may see it as units that are added along the number line. When we add positive numbers, we count to the right on a number line. When we add negative numbers, we count to the left on a number line.
  • Subtracting a number is the same as adding the "opposite" of the number. For example, is the same as .
  • Subtraction may also be seen as the difference between two numbers. For example, there are 5 units between the numbers 2 and 7. If the number which is subtracted from lies to the negative side of the number that is subtracted, the difference is negative: . If the number which is subtracted from lies to the positive side of the number that is subtracted, the difference is positive: .
  • A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature. Temperatures above are positive. Temperatures below are negative.
  • A positive bank balance means you have money in the bank. A negative bank balance means you owe the bank money.
  • For movement along a straight line, we take one direction as positive. The opposite direction is negative.
records.content_text:
- The place value of a digit tells us what the value of that digit is, based on its position in a number.
- When we add or subtract large numbers, we line up the units, tens, hundreds and thousands of the numbers.
- A number line is a straight line, divided into equal segments, that shows the positions of numbers.
- Positive numbers are larger than zero and lie to the right of zero on a number line.
- Negative numbers are smaller than zero and lie to the left of zero on a number line.
- Zero is neither positive nor negative.
- The symbol < means "smaller than", and 3<5 means three is smaller than five. The symbol > means "greater than", and 5>3 means five is greater than three.
- When we add one integer to another, we may see it as units that are added along the number line. When we add positive numbers, we count to the right on a number line. When we add negative numbers, we count to the left on a number line.
- Subtracting a number is the same as adding the "opposite" of the number. For example, $2-7$ is the same as $2+(-7)$.
- Subtraction may also be seen as the difference between two numbers. For example, there are 5 units between the numbers 2 and 7. If the number which is subtracted from lies to the negative side of the number that is subtracted, the difference is negative: $2-7=-5$. If the number which is subtracted from lies to the positive side of the number that is subtracted, the difference is positive: $7-2=5$.
- A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature. Temperatures above $0\space ^\circ\text C$ are positive. Temperatures below $0\space ^\circ\text C$ are negative.
- A positive bank balance means you have money in the bank. A negative bank balance means you owe the bank money.
- For movement along a straight line, we take one direction as positive. The opposite direction is negative.

There is $\frac{3}{4}$ of the cake left:

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-06-036.png)

Danladi did not have any cake yet. He gets 1 piece, which is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the cake:

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-06-005.png)

After Danladi took his piece, $\frac{2}{4}$ of the cake is left:

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-06-037.png)

We write this as:

$$
\frac{3}{4}-\frac{1}{4}=\frac{2}{4}
$$
The simplest form of $\frac{2}{4}$ is $\frac{1}{2}$.

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-06-006.png)

We may therefore write:

$$
\frac{3}{4}-\frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{2}
$$

Worked example 6.1: Adding fractions with the same denominator

Calculate:

  1. Method 1 (Using diagrams)

    1. The denominator shows into how many parts one whole must be divided. Represent this in a diagram. In this case, there must be 10 parts.

    2. Shade the number of parts shown by the first numerator. The first numerator is 7.

    3. Now also shade the number of parts shown by the second numerator. The second numerator is 1. We must shade another 1 part.

  2. Method 2 (Calculating directly)

    1. The denominator shows into how many parts one whole must be divided. Write down the denominator.

    2. Write down the numerators that must be added.
